content:
Two months ago, we reported on three cases involving apps belonging to a US-sanctioned Russian bank appearing on the App Store under different guises. Now, another similar example has shot to the top of the iPhone App Store charts.

The latest case is K8CHEN PRO. On its App Store listing page, it disguises itself as a kitchen design tool with augmented reality (AR) capabilities.

But the moment you open the app, the cracks immediately show. The privacy policy link on the App Store page reveals that its content was auto-generated by "Free Privacy Policy Generator" — that alone is a massive red flag.

Regardless, this app is unmistakably a client for T-Bank. What baffles me is how these apps keep passing App Store review.

When these apps skyrocket up the App Store rankings because they've gone viral, anyone with eyes can see they should never have been allowed on the store in the first place. It's truly baffling.

As for the other cases reported in June, you can read about them here and here.

Update: Sure enough, the app has now been pulled from the App Store.
